curriculum.lesson_evidence: The beat is the steady pulse in music, like a heartbeat. We can find the beat by clapping, tapping or stepping along. Tempo is how fast or slow the beat is. Moving to a beat means stepping, clapping or moving in time with it. Counting 1, 2, 3, 4 helps. Dance in a clear space, listen carefully and move safely around others.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A song has 4 beats in each group. Describe a simple movement pattern that uses all four beats and changes on beat 4.

FEEDBACK
Pattern: step, step, step, clap on beat 4. Counting aloud helps keep time. Changing on beat 4 marks the end of each group.

WATCH FOR
Thinking the beat is the words of the song. The beat is the steady pulse underneath, which stays the same while the words change.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Choose two songs with different tempos. Clap the beat of each, count the beats in a group and make a four-beat movement pattern for each. Record how the pattern changes with tempo and teach one to a family member.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: listen to a song and find the beat by clapping on every beat: 1 2 3 4. Then step to the beat: step, step, step, step. Change the tempo: with a slower song take slow steps, with a faster song take quick steps. Kofi counts '1, 2, 3, 4' out loud and moves his arms on count 4.

TRY FIRST
A song has 4 beats in each group. Describe a simple movement pattern that uses all four beats and changes on beat 4.

FEEDBACK
Pattern: step, step, step, clap on beat 4. Counting aloud helps keep time. Changing on beat 4 marks the end of each group.
teach_steps.explain:
The beat is the steady pulse in music, like a heartbeat. We can find the beat by clapping, tapping or stepping along. Tempo is how fast or slow the beat is. Moving to a beat means stepping, clapping or moving in time with it. Counting 1, 2, 3, 4 helps. Dance in a clear space, listen carefully and move safely around others.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
